summary_paragraph: A woman with Hb-SS disease was admitted for a severe vaso-occlusive pain crisis involving her knees, shoulders, hips, and chest. She developed acute chest syndrome with hypoxemia and bilateral pulmonary infiltrates, prompting transfer to the MICU. A central venous catheter was placed, and she underwent exchange transfusion to reduce sickle hemoglobin. She was treated with antibiotics for suspected pneumonia after developing a fever, though cultures were negative. Pain was managed with a PCA pump and transitioned to oral hydromorphone. Constipation was addressed with stool softeners, and lisinopril was restarted for proteinuria. Her condition improved, with resolution of infiltrates and stabilization of labs. She was discharged home on oral medications including levofloxacin, Dilaudid, and hydroxyurea, with follow-up arranged.
